En 2025, l’or s’est imposé comme l’une des catégories d’actifs les plus rentables.  Mais qu’est-ce qui explique cette envolée ? Découvrez dans cette vidéo les cinq facteurs clés expliqués par Jordan, allant d’un dollar américain plus faible aux achats des banques centrales.

Transcription :

Bonjour à tous ! Je suis content de vous retrouver sur cette chaîne. Aujourd’hui, je vous parle rapidement des éléments qui ont soutenu le prix de l’or depuis le début de l’année. L’or ne rapporte pas de dividendes, ne génère pas de bénéfices et ne verse pas d’intérêts. Et pourtant, en 2025, il a été l’une des catégories d’actifs les plus performantes, affichant une hausse de plus de 65 % jusqu’à présent. L’or reste un élément clé d’un portefeuille bien diversifié. Beaucoup d’investisseurs considèrent l’or comme une valeur refuge, un moyen de se protéger contre l’inflation et une alternative à la monnaie classique. Avec la forte hausse de l’or cette année, examinons rapidement les forces qui influencent son cours. Tout d’abord, la faiblesse du dollar américain : l’or est coté en dollars, donc quand le dollar perd de la valeur, l’or monte généralement. En 2025, le dollar a un peu perdu de terrain, ce qui a soutenu les prix de l’or. 

Ensuite, l’inflation. Elle s’est calmée depuis son sommet, mais elle est toujours bien présente, surtout avec l’effet inflationniste des droits de douane. Résultat : les craintes inflationnistes ont continué de soutenir l’or cette année.  Un autre facteur clé est la baisse des taux d’intérêt. Étant donné que l’or ne génère ni dividendes ni revenus d’intérêts, une baisse des taux réduit le coût d’opportunité de sa détention, ce qui le rend plus attrayant pour les investisseurs. L’incertitude et la volatilité des marchés ont toujours soutenu le prix de l’or. Qu’il s’agisse de tensions géopolitiques, de droits de douane, d’élections ou de fluctuations des marchés, ces facteurs ont tendance à favoriser l’or. Cette année, en particulier, les investisseurs ont privilégié les catégories d’actif qui ne dépendent ni des prévisions de bénéfices ni de la croissance économique pour générer des rendements. Le rôle de valeur refuge de l’or, ou de couverture contre l’incertitude, s’est clairement illustré cette année. 

Pour finir, parlons des banques centrales. Elles achètent de l’or pour diversifier leurs réserves et moins dépendre du dollar américain. Comme ce sont des acheteurs stratégiques, elles se soucient beaucoup moins des fluctuations de prix à court terme. Bref, 2025 s’est distinguée comme une année remarquable pour l’or, porté par la faiblesse du dollar américain, la baisse des taux d’intérêt, une inflation persistante, une incertitude élevée et une demande continue des banques centrales.

title: The 2025 Year in Review, Part 6: RBC Heritage, Zurich, Byron Nelson, & Truist | The Shotgun Start
description:
Despite the almost four-hour runtime of Part 5, the show must go on as the self-imposed Christmas deadline inches closer and closer. Andy and Brendan are once again joined by PJ and KVV to chat through a set of four events following Rory's win at the Masters. Before the Year in Review gets back underway, the four recap this week's biggest news: Alejandro Tosti's performance at PGA Tour Q-School. Everyone is giddy to have Tosti back for another season on the big tour and they commend him for fighting through Q-School for a second time. Andy, Brendan, and Kevin also discuss some late-breaking golf news regarding the National Links Trust and the Trump administration's plan to renovate the three public golf courses in Washington D.C. The Year in Review resumes with a look back at the RBC Heritage and the immediate wake of one of the greatest wins in golf history. PJ runs through a week's worth of Rory reactions before unveiling the important stuff, such as Grant Horvat's Barracuda exemption (unused) and Wesley Bryan's PGA Tour suspension (still seemingly ongoing). Justin Thomas returned to the winner's circle in Hilton Head, getting over the finish line for the first time since the 2022 PGA Championship. Andy is next up with the Zurich Classic, where Rory McIlroy made his return to golf in a team event alongside Shane Lowry. Andy rediscovers the backboarding that occurred at a disastrous Chevron Championship and the power outage that led to the golf world being exposed to a Champions Tour Sunday on national TV. He also shares that one of the great technological achievements of our time happened this week! Brendan has the honor of recapping PGA Tour history, as Scottie Scheffler burned down TPC Craig T. Nelson Ranch and tied the all-time scoring record in a runaway win. All that may be great, but Brendan is most excited about the children in attendance chanting while a bulldozer wrecked the practice green ahead of Lanny's renovation. KVV comes in to close things out again, handling the first-ever Truist Championship. His findings lead the group down a rabbit-hole of past HSBC photo shoots, complete with a flying Henrik Stenson and Yao Ming. The 2025 Year in Review returns on Wednesday with the long-awaited Rise of Rea.

title: Supply Demand Trading Tips✅
description:
Supply and demand zones are areas on a chart where price made a strong move after a period of consolidation. This consolidation, often called basing, is where the market pauses and builds orders before making an explosive move up or down.

A demand zone forms when price bases and then rallies aggressively, showing strong buying interest. A supply zone forms when price bases and then drops sharply, indicating strong selling pressure.

Traders mark these basing areas as zones because when price returns to them, there’s a higher chance it will react again. Instead of chasing price, we place limit orders at these zones and wait for price to pull back, allowing us to enter trades with better risk-to-reward.

This approach is all about patience—letting price come to you and trading from key areas where institutions have likely made their moves.

Supply and demand zones are areas on a chart where price made a strong move after a period of consolidation. This consolidation, often called basing, is where the market pauses and builds orders before making an explosive move up or down.

A demand zone forms when price bases and then rallies aggressively, showing strong buying interest. A supply zone forms when price bases and then drops sharply, indicating strong selling pressure.

Traders mark these basing areas as zones because when price returns to them, there’s a higher chance it will react again. Instead of chasing price, we place limit orders at these zones and wait for price to pull back, allowing us to enter trades with better risk-to-reward.

This approach is all about patience—letting price come to you and trading from key areas where institutions have likely made their moves.

title: Fundamental Analysis is BULLSH*T! | Trading Psychology
description:
In this episode we break down why fundamental analysis is mostly useless for traders and why so many traders rely on it for the wrong reasons. Most traders are taking 2:1 or 3:1 risk-to-reward trades, which means predicting the economy or reading news headlines isn’t what determines profitability. What actually matters is risk management, positioning, and understanding how price moves around key levels.

We talk about why market narratives constantly change, why news rarely gives precise entries, and why price often reacts at technical areas like supply and demand zones regardless of the fundamental story. If you’ve ever wondered why traders obsess over news while still losing money, this episode explains what really drives consistent trading results.

This is an episode from the Stoic Trading Psychology Podcast, where we dive deep into the mental side of trading. In each episode, we explore the principles of discipline, patience, emotional control, and stoic philosophy, all of which are key to building consistency and longevity in the markets. Trading psychology isn’t just important, it’s the foundation of success. Without mastering your mindset, no strategy will ever work in the long run.

If you want to improve your trading psychology, gain clarity in your decision making, and learn how to approach the markets like a disciplined professional, this podcast will help you get there.
